step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture shows Arc Publishing's web rendering platform at The Washington Post. Public web traffic arrives at an origin router running on ECS. If static assets or pre-rendered HTML are not found in the respective S3 buckets, the request triggers a Lambda function for dynamic rendering (5-10% cache miss rate). A secondary ECS service acts as a content proxy, retrieving content from external CMS/APIs and caching raw JSON objects in ElastiCache with a TTL. Newsroom users create page templates saved to DynamoDB, while developers deploy rendering code updates directly to AWS Lambda.

edges.notes: Public users send web requests to the origin ECS cluster.
Origin ECS fetches static JavaScript and CSS resources from S3.
Origin ECS checks S3 for pre-rendered HTML page content.
Cache misses trigger Lambda to dynamically render the requested web page.
Lambda queries DynamoDB for page template layout definitions.
Lambda writes rendered pages to the pre-rendered content S3 bucket.
Content proxy ECS fetches stories, galleries, and media from external CMS / APIs.
Content proxy stores raw content JSON objects into ElastiCache with a TTL.
Newsroom users define and write web templates directly into DynamoDB.
Developers deploy web rendering JavaScript code deployments into Lambda.
